reason: Internal: design bundle only, no code. Resolves what Step 1 of design/evaluation/ is actually asking, by measurement rather than by argument. All three candidate homes for the single subject function were probed by injecting the imports it needs — nora.app.composition, nora.infra.sql, nora.config — and running lint-imports. nora.testing breaks one, one and two contracts respectively, the first being a reverse import into the top layer. nora/app/ is legal and is exactly where the bundle says eval-only code must not live. A new top-level package passes both lint-imports and tests/test_boundaries.py clean while importing all three at once — not because that was decided but because root_packages is nora and evals only and the boundary test scans the evals directory only, so a third package is outside both and nothing looks. That is a hole rather than a solution: taking it requires adding the package to root_packages and writing its contract, and writing that contract is Step 1 itself. The finding underneath is that the layer architecture has no slot for a thing that obtains the real Nora and is not the application, which is why nora/app/offline.py exists, why it drifted into a second assembly, and why eval_support.py is 1,739 lines of test scaffolding inside the application package — none of which were mistakes given the available slots. Step 1 therefore asks for a layer, not a directory, with three legal options stated and priced, and nothing else in the bundle can start until it is answered.
